claim: Tennessee's execution protocol uses pentobarbital as a single-drug method.
Primary Set A contains approximately 5 g pentobarbital in total.
The protocol contains a Backup Set B if the prisoner remains alive after Set A and the required waiting/examination step.
Pike's pre-execution discovery specifically raised the lack of medical care, resuscitation or emergency intervention after a failed execution.
source: U.S. Supreme Court docket 26-5696 Appendix A Part 2, Request for Admission No. 7
notes: This is a documented request by Pike's side; not characterized here as a state admission.

claim: Pike's Request for Admission No. 7 described Backup Set B as the protocol's only contingency after Set A and a five-minute waiting period.
source: U.S. Supreme Court docket 26-5696 Appendix A Part 2

claim: TDOC said it followed every step of the state's established execution protocol on 2026-09-30.
TDOC said the protocol did not allow additional procedures beyond those carried out that evening.
TDOC said Pike was transported to an off-site medical facility.
Contemporary reporting states that both the primary and backup pentobarbital administrations were used and Pike remained alive.
source: AP / Tennessee Lookout / other contemporaneous reporting
notes: Cross-check against official review when available.

claim: Tennessee's Carruthers execution attempt in May 2026 was abandoned after required IV access could not be completed.
source: Governor of Tennessee statement and subsequent court filings

claim: Governor Bill Lee ordered a third-party review after Pike's failed execution attempt.
Tennessee halted remaining executions for the rest of 2026.
The full intended pentobarbital dose reached Pike's systemic circulation as intended.
notes: Do not infer from syringe administration alone.

claim: IV infiltration or IV failure caused the unsuccessful execution.
Drug preparation or potency caused the unsuccessful execution.
An unusual physiological response caused the unsuccessful execution.
Pentobarbital itself was pharmacologically ineffective.
Before the execution, the Tennessee Supreme Court decision expressly identified Pike's challenge that the protocol did not provide medical care or resuscitation in the event of a failed execution.
notes: Confirms the issue was litigated before 2026-09-30; does not itself establish the merits of Pike's constitutional claim.

claim: Riverbend Warden Kenneth Nelson testified under oath that he was familiar with the protocol, had overseen four executions, supervised the execution process, and had not been involved in discussions about contingency plans such as placing a central line for Pike.
source: U.S. Supreme Court docket 26-5696 Appendix B, Aug. 11, 2026 evidentiary hearing
notes: Supports pre-execution contingency-planning analysis; does not establish the contents of any separate undisclosed emergency plan.

claim: The State's counsel argued at the Aug. 11 evidentiary hearing that expert opinions concerning post-execution resuscitation were irrelevant and outside the scope of the expert's testimony.
source: U.S. Supreme Court docket 26-5696 Appendix B, Aug. 11, 2026 evidentiary hearing
notes: Procedural litigation position; not equivalent to an admission that no resuscitation plan existed.

claim: Before Pike's execution, the Tennessee Supreme Court expressly addressed her challenge to the protocol's lack of a resuscitation provision and held that she was unlikely to succeed on that claim.
notes: Confirms that the post-failure/resuscitation issue was squarely before the court before the execution.

claim: Pike's attorneys reported a blood clot, pneumonia, and severe swelling in her arms and hands after the failed execution.
notes: Medical status reported by counsel; primary medical records not public.

claim: A Davidson County Chancery judge ordered Tennessee officials to preserve all evidence related to Pike's failed execution.
notes: State counsel said the State was already planning preservation.

claim: Former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton was named to lead the independent review of the failed execution.
TDOC Commissioner Frank Strada is resigning following the failed execution.
notes: Resignation announced by Gov. Bill Lee.

notes: Causal mechanism remains unresolved; do not upgrade without primary evidence.
